title: Dedicated Capacity HUD: Compact Health + Gesture Controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, single-row HUD for Dedicated capacity pools that surfaces critical GPU pool health signals, quick autoscale controls, and one-tap burst configuration. The HUD must be readable across dense fleet lists, support keyboard and touch gestures for rapid ops, and degrade gracefully to a detailed panel for troubleshooting. This ticket covers interaction design, high-fidelity screens, an accessibility pass, and a handoff-ready spec for frontend engineers and product managers.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity HUD prototype linked in Figma with annotated states (healthy, warming, degraded, burst-active)
Interaction spec describing keyboard shortcuts, swipe/tap gestures, and confirmation flows for scale/burst actions
Accessibility checklist completed (contrast, focus order, ARIA roles, screen-reader behaviors)
Engineering-ready tokens and spacing system exported and validated with FE during handoff
Design review approval from PM (Miguel Torres) and Eng lead (Sophia Ramirez)
decisions: Use compact health bar with three micro-indicators (latency, throughput, error-rate) instead of full charts to preserve scanability in list views
Primary autoscale control will be a two-state quick toggle (Auto / Manual) and a short-press opens the detailed autoscale composer
Burst will be a contextual inline control that opens a modal for duration & target capacity; immediate one-tap 5m burst option included for emergencies
Keyboard: 'h' toggles HUD focus, arrow keys navigate pools, Enter opens detailed panel; Escape closes modals
To avoid accidental scale operations, require a second confirmation for burst > 15 minutes or capacity > 2x current
tradeoffs: Compact micro-indicators favor scanability but lose historical trend context; resolved by linking to the detailed timeline panel on click
Inline burst controls may increase surface area for accidental clicks; mitigated by introducing tolerant tap zones plus confirmation for risky inputs
Keyboard-focused interactions improve operator speed but add accessibility testing overhead across screen readers and keyboard-only flows
